1.name: Volute casing
1.note: The spiral housing round the impeller. It widens towards the discharge and so turns the water's speed into pressure.

2.name: Impeller
2.note: The rotating wheel that flings the water outwards. Its speed sets the pump curve through the affinity laws.

3.name: Casing wear ring
3.note: A replaceable ring that keeps a small gap round the impeller eye, so little water leaks back to the suction.

4.name: Impeller cap nut
4.note: Locks the impeller on the end of the shaft. Its dome keeps the flow into the eye smooth.

5.name: Key
5.note: Transmits the shaft's torque to the impeller.

6.name: Pump shaft
6.note: Carries the motor's rotation from the coupling to the impeller.

7.name: Casing gasket
7.note: Seals the joint between the casing and the casing cover.

8.name: Casing cover
8.note: Closes the back of the volute and houses the mechanical seal.

9.name: Rotary seal unit
9.note: The rotating half of the mechanical seal. Its carbon face runs against the seat and stops water escaping along the shaft.

10.name: Seal seat
10.note: The hard stationary face that the rotary unit runs on.

11.name: O-ring
11.note: Seals the seal seat in the casing cover.

12.name: Hex bolt
12.note: Clamps the casing cover and the casing to the bearing bracket.

13.name: Bearing bracket
13.note: The housing that holds the bearings and carries the pump on its foot.

14.name: V-ring
14.note: A thrower on the shaft that flings leaked water away before it reaches the bearings.

15.name: Ball bearing
15.note: Supports the shaft and takes the impeller's radial and axial loads.

16.name: Retaining ring
16.note: A circlip on the shaft that locates the bearing.

17.name: Bearing cover
17.note: Closes the bearing housing at the drive end.

18.name: Shaft seal
18.note: A lip seal where the shaft leaves the bearing housing, keeping the grease in and dirt out.

19.name: Cap screw
19.note: Holds the bearing cover to the bracket.

20.name: Coupling hub
20.note: The pump half of the flexible coupling. It is keyed to the shaft.

21.name: Coupling spider
21.note: A soft insert between the two coupling halves. It takes up small misalignment and damps vibration.

22.name: Key
22.note: Joins the coupling hub to the shaft.

23.name: Drain plug
23.note: Lets you empty the casing for service.

24.name: Valve body
24.note: The globe valve housing on the discharge. Its S-shaped passage forces the flow past the seat.

25.name: Valve plug
25.note: The throttle. Closing it narrows the gap, which steepens the system curve and moves the duty point to a lower flow.

26.name: Valve stem
26.note: A trapezoidal screw that turns the handwheel into plug travel.

27.name: Bonnet with yoke
27.note: The valve's cover. It guides the stem and houses the packing.

28.name: Packing ring
28.note: Rings round the stem that seal it against leakage.

29.name: Gland follower
29.note: Presses the packing rings to keep the stem sealed.

30.name: Handwheel
30.note: You turn it to throttle the discharge. It is the control for the system curve.
